rows.description: A client barely reads your work and asks for changes without engaging. It feels demoralising. Ask direct questions, pin down decisions, and do not internalise their disinterest as a verdict on your quality.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, exploitation, fear, loyalty, manipulation, protectiveness

rows.description: A notice from the tax office makes your heart race and imagination run wild. Read it carefully, note deadlines, gather documents, and consult a qualified professional. Panic-paying agents or ignoring it worsens things.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: exploitation, guilt, resentment, respect, shame, trust

rows.description: Treat the process as a system with rules, not a personal attack. Respond on time, be accurate, and be polite in writing. Dealing honestly with authority usually costs less than hiding.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: exploitation, fear, guilt, resentment, shame, trust

rows.description: Someone offers to make the problem vanish for a fee and shortcuts. Recognise a common exploit: bribery is illegal and leaves you exposed and owned. Use certified professionals and official portals, and ask for receipts.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: fear, guilt, resentment, respect, shame, trust

rows.description: Rules feel unfair and complex, and you resent paying. It is fine to dislike a system while complying with it and voting or advocating for change. Evasion turns a grievance into a legal risk.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: exploitation, fear, guilt, respect, shame, trust

rows.description: You fear parents' judgment about the notice or a legal case. Tell them early, since secrecy adds stress and lets small issues grow. Families often help more than expected when they are told plainly.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: exploitation, fear, guilt, resentment, respect, trust

rows.description: A good adviser explains options and risks and does not promise guaranteed outcomes. Trust them with full facts. Hiding details or expecting miracles leads to poor results and blaming them later.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: exploitation, fear, guilt, resentment, respect, shame

rows.description: You made a genuine error in filing and feel like a criminal. Voluntary correction is usually better than concealment. Own the mistake, fix it, keep records going forward, and forgive yourself for being new at adulthood.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: exploitation, fear, resentment, respect, shame, trust

rows.description: Facing a police officer or an official office triggers dread, especially after stories of harassment. Stay calm, know your rights, carry documents, be polite, and ask for names and receipts. Do not argue or offer a bribe.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, coercion, compassion, disillusionment, manipulation, trust

rows.description: An officer pressures you to pay or sign something you did not read. Recognise the coercion, keep calm, do not sign blindly, ask to contact a lawyer or family, and later file a complaint through proper channels. It is not your fault.
